Opposite page: The "last" Belgrave-Southern Relay.
Top. High noon and the starter sends 61 runners off on the first leg. Jon Hobbs completes his lap of the "top" and nears the crowd at the Hand in Hand.
Centre. Ollie Foote sends Marcello Bizio away on the last stage. Jim Estall loosens up for the London Marathon with a 25:53 long leg. Second fastest long stage of the day and another mark in the all-time top 20 - Paul Evans has an easy run!
Bottom. Jim Estall launches Marco Mazzotta. Frank Ward reaches the summit of Wool Road. Putting on a good show for visiting relations, "Aussie" Brandon Reid streaks off the Common for a nippy second leg.

Back page: In spite of having run the Surrey League CC Race less than 24 hours earlier, when it came to the Epsom Marathon Windows 10 miles Jim Estall was never headed and he won from some 400 runners in 53:15. It's been a great few months for Jim culminating in his London Marathon run where he was third scorer in our winning team.

Wearing the English Rose, M40 Jim Estall (220) grafts away at the head of the Home Countries International Veterans' Cross Country Champs. at Ballymena on November 8th.  It's the fourth of  five laps and still no-one has been able to dominate the field.  However, the tattooed Rob Wise, close up behind Jim at this point, was soon to make a decisive move.  Gerry Brady (211) of Ireland was unable to respond while Mike Hagar and Jim gave chase.  On the final lap the Belgravian overtook Hagar to gain a clear 2nd in 31:55 but Wise at 31:37 was out of reach.

A super start to the Surrey League series came from last winter's individual winner Jim Estall. Unfortunately Jim was not able to contest all four League races as match two clashed with the British & Irish Veterans' International 10k Cross Country race at St. Asaph, Wales, where Jim led the England M40 team to victory.
Rob Harding, Ray Foley, Mike Webb, Clive Gilby, Kevin Quinn, Jim Estall John Mather and Lee Hurst steel themselves for the start of the first Surrey League race of 1998-99.
